1	FIG. 1 shows a charging installation 100 in which several electric vehicles are charged from one electrical branch. A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity. The branch current limit is lower than a sum of the current ratings of the vehicle connectors served by the branch conductor 102, so that the connectors cannot all deliver their rated current at the same time and the aggregate current is governed by control rather than by the rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A first connector channel 120 and a second connector channel 140 are connected to the branch conductor 102 in parallel. Two connector channels are shown for clarity of illustration. Any number of connector channels of two or more may be connected to the branch conductor 102, and the description of the first connector channel 120 applies to each further connector channel, the second connector channel 140 being of the same construction. A non-charging load 118 is also connected to the branch conductor 102 and represents the equipment of the site that shares the branch and whose current the controller does not command.
4	
5	A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current, that is, the total current carried by the branch conductor 102. Because the branch current sensor 104 is upstream of every connector channel and of the non-charging load 118, its measurement is independent of the measurements made within the connector channels and is not affected by a failure, a miswiring or a scaling error in any one connector channel. 36

40

44	
45	The allocation interval and the verification interval are stored configuration values of the edge controller 106, the allocation interval being short enough that a change in the non-charging load 118 or in vehicle demand is answered before it can carry the branch above the branch current limit for an appreciable time.
46	
47	The vehicle connectors may be of any type that carries control pilot signalling.
48	
49	The foregoing describes particular embodiments. A person skilled in the art will recognize that features described with reference to one embodiment may be combined with features described with reference to another, and that the invention is not limited to the particular embodiments described.

1	Parking structures, fleet depots, workplaces and multi unit dwellings commonly install several electric vehicle connectors on a single electrical branch. The conductors, overcurrent device and upstream transformer capacity of that branch are sized for an aggregate current that is lower, and often much lower, than the sum of the individual current ratings of the connectors served by it. The installation therefore depends on a control function that continuously divides the branch capacity among the connectors that are in use, rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.
2	
3	A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit to each vehicle over a control pilot signalling interface. The limit is advisory in the sense that it is a request addressed to equipment that the site operator does not own and cannot inspect. A vehicle may respond slowly, may respond only in coarse steps, may hold a previous current for an interval after a new limit is signalled, or may not follow the signalled limit at all. Auxiliary equipment on the same branch, such as lighting, ventilation, elevators or refrigeration, draws current that the charging control function does not command and that changes without notice. A control function that computes an allocation and then assumes the allocation has taken effect can therefore hold the branch above its rated aggregate current while every connector believes it is compliant, with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection. Tripping that device removes every charging session on the branch at once, and in many installations it also removes the auxiliary loads sharing the branch.
4	
5	Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization. Connectivity in a below grade parking structure or a remote depot is intermittent. A controller that treats loss of connectivity as a reason to stop charging strands vehicles that were already authorized, while a controller that treats loss of connectivity as permission to charge without restraint abandons the branch limit that the last accepted configuration established, and abandons the accounting record that billing depends on.
6	
7	A further difficulty arises at installation. The connector identifier used by the control function, the physical contactor that energizes a connector and the current sensing channel that measures it are joined by field wiring performed once, often by a contractor who does not operate the equipment afterwards. If that wiring map is recorded incorrectly, the control function will deliver a computed current limit to one connector while measuring another. Every subsequent verification appears to succeed, because the two errors are consistent with one another, and the fault is discovered only when the branch overcurrent device operates or when a vehicle receives a limit that was intended for a different vehicle.
8	
9	There remains a need for a controller that treats the aggregate current of the branch as a measured quantity, verified independently of the per connector measurements and independently of any vehicle response, and that converts an unanswered current reduction into a bounded, ordered and recoverable removal of load rather than into an uncontrolled trip of the branch overcurrent device.

Every numeral in numerals.md is used for one part only and appears in exactly one consistent role in the detailed description and in a figure brief; 100/102/104/106/108/118/120/140 on FIG. 1, 108/120/122/124/126/128/130 on FIG. 2, 106/110/112/114/116/132/134 on FIG. 3, 202-216 on FIG. 4, with no numeral labelling two different parts. The claim-word warning is a false positive (the missing words are the token "claim" from dependent-claim references).

Three defects are reported: one added, self-contradicting statement about where the branch current limit comes from; one term ("staged reduction") used for two different steps; and one apparatus claim that operates an element it never recites. All three have local, source-supported fixes.

findings.title: Detailed description says the branch current limit is received over the network interface, which the disclosure does not state and which contradicts the same section's own definition of that limit
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph at line 37 (and paragraph at line 1)
findings.detail: The disclosure confines the network interface to remote schedules and authorizations: "The controller can receive remote schedules and authorizations through a network interface, but it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory." It never says the branch limit itself arrives over the network. The candidate adds that origin, and the addition collides with the candidate's own opening definition of the branch current limit as a physical property of the installation. As written the document gives the branch current limit two mutually exclusive sources — the conductor/overcurrent-device/supply rating in paragraph 1, and a value most recently received over the network in paragraph 37 — and the reader cannot tell which quantity claims 1, 9, 14 and 18 allocate against. Note that the summary (draft/06-summary.md line 9) and claims 9 and 18 stay neutral ("to hold a signed local authorization token and a last accepted branch limit in the nonvolatile memory"), so the unsupported assertion is local to this paragraph and can be removed without disturbing the claims. Paragraph 1's list of what fixes the limit ("by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity") is likewise not in the disclosure, which says only "one electrical branch whose allowable aggregate current is lower than the sum of the connector ratings"; the two passages together are what produce the contradiction.
findings.evidence: Paragraph 37: "The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently received and accepted through the network interface 110, retained so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against." Paragraph 1: "A branch conductor 102 supplies the installation and has a branch current limit, that is, an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity." Disclosure: "The controller can receive remote schedules and authorizations through a network interface, but it stores a signed local authorization token and the last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory."
findings.fix: In paragraph 37 delete the network origin and keep only the disclosed retention function: replace "The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently received and accepted through the network interface 110, retained so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against." with "The last accepted branch limit is the branch current limit most recently accepted by the edge controller 106, retained in the nonvolatile memory 112 so that a loss of the network does not leave the edge controller 106 without a limit to allocate against." In paragraph 1 replace "an allowable aggregate current fixed by the rating of the branch conductor 102, by the overcurrent device protecting it and by the upstream supply capacity" with "an allowable aggregate current of the branch conductor 102", matching the disclosure's wording.

findings.title: "Staged reduction" names two different steps of FIG. 4
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraphs at lines 25 and 27; draft/numerals.md line 28; draft/07-drawings.md line 7
findings.detail: The connector-level response at the connector verification step 208 is expressly labelled "the staged reduction of the allocation", while numeral 210 is separately defined in numerals.md and in the detailed description as "staged reduction step 210", a different step performing a different comparison (measured branch current against the branch current limit). The Brief Description of the Drawings uses the same phrase again for FIG. 4 as a whole. One name is therefore attached to two distinct numbered operations, and a reader following "the staged reduction" cannot tell whether step 208 or step 210 is meant. The disclosure uses the phrase once, for the pilot-signalling stage that precedes shedding ("staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond"), so the fix is to reserve the labelled name for step 210 and describe step 208's action as its first stage.
findings.evidence: Line 25: "This is the staged reduction of the allocation, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed." Line 27: "At a staged reduction step 210, the edge controller 106 compares the measured branch current from the branch current sensor 104 with the branch current limit." numerals.md: "| 210 | staged reduction step |"
findings.fix: In the paragraph at line 25 replace "This is the staged reduction of the allocation, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed." with "This is a first stage of the reduction of the allocation, continued at the staged reduction step 210 described below, and it is the first response of the edge controller 106 to a connector channel that is drawing more than it has been allowed."

findings.title: Claim 5 requires the controller to operate a local fault indicator that the apparatus claim never recites
findings.detail: Claim 5 is an apparatus claim depending from claim 1. It recites a function performed on "a local fault indicator", but neither claim 1 nor claim 5 includes that indicator among the elements of the apparatus, so the claimed apparatus is required to operate a component it does not comprise. The parallel dependent claims in this set do it the other way and introduce their hardware properly — claim 8 "further comprising an isolated local bus", claim 9 "further comprising a network interface and a nonvolatile memory", claim 12 "further comprising a service input" — which shows the omission is a drafting slip rather than a deliberate scope choice. The element is fully described ("A fault indicator 116 is a local fault indicator at the installation and is operated by the processing unit 132"), so the correction needs no new matter. Method claim 17 is unaffected, because a method step may operate an indicator without reciting it as a component.
findings.evidence: Claim 5: "The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition ... and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate a local fault indicator." Compare claim 8: "The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an isolated local bus coupling the controller ..."
findings.fix: Recast claim 5 as: "The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a local fault indicator, wherein the controller is further configured to record a welded-contactor condition when the connector current of a connector channel remains above a leakage threshold after an open command has been issued to the contactor of that connector channel, and, responsive to the recorded welded-contactor condition, to inhibit the contactors of the other connector channels of the plurality of connector channels and to operate the local fault indicator."
